passage: Counselling note, by Jeevan. Anirban came in on Tuesday with two offer letters and a nervous grin. He told me he was thinking of saying his previous internship stipend had been higher, "just to bargain harder". He looked at the desk while he said it, and his knee was bouncing. I asked whether he knew that companies often check with the earlier employer. He had not thought of that. I told him a false number can cost him the offer later, even after he joins. We then spent half an hour listing what he actually brings: the two projects, the tools he knows, how similar roles are paid. He said he would name a figure based on that. He left looking less tense. I will ask him next week how the conversation went.

qa.q: When did Anirban come to see Jeevan?
What do Anirban's downcast eyes and bouncing knee suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: They suggest he felt uneasy and a little ashamed about the idea of lying, even while he was tempted by the extra bargaining power.

qa.q: What could Anirban do instead of inflating his previous stipend?
qa.a: He can anchor his request on the value of his skills and projects and how similar roles are paid, and stay honest about his past.

qa.q: How might the employer see a false previous salary if it were discovered?
qa.a: The employer may see it as dishonesty and lose trust in Anirban, and the offer could be withdrawn. Jeevan says a false number can cost the offer later.

grounding: The protagonist is tempted to inflate his previous salary to bargain harder, and is guided to honesty and anchoring on the market value of his skills.
